question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.

prediction.sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
  SELECT a.ArtistId, a.Name, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
  FROM artists a
  JOIN albums al ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
  JOIN tracks t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
),
top_artist AS (
  SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales DESC, Name ASC LIMIT 1
),
low_artist AS (
  SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales ASC, Name ASC LIMIT 1
),
cust_spend AS (
  SELECT inv.CustomerId,
    SUM(CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist) THEN ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS top_spend,
    SUM(CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM low_artist) THEN ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS low_spend
  FROM invoice_items ii
  JOIN invoices inv ON inv.InvoiceId = ii.InvoiceId
  JOIN tracks t ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
  JOIN albums al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY inv.CustomerId
),
top_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(top_spend) AS avg_top FROM cust_spend WHERE top_spend > 0
),
low_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(low_spend) AS avg_low FROM cust_spend WHERE low_spend > 0
)
SELECT ABS((SELECT avg_top FROM top_avg) - (SELECT avg_low FROM low_avg)) AS abs_diff

base_solution_anchor.base_sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
  SELECT a.ArtistId, a.Name, SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
  FROM artists a
  JOIN albums al ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
  JOIN tracks t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN invoice_items ii ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY a.ArtistId, a.Name
),
top AS (SELECT ArtistId FROM (SELECT ArtistId, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC, Name ASC) rn FROM artist_sales) WHERE rn=1),
low AS (SELECT ArtistId FROM (SELECT ArtistId, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales ASC, Name ASC) rn FROM artist_sales) WHERE rn=1),
cust_spend AS (
  SELECT inv.CustomerId,
    CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top) THEN 'top'
         WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM low) THEN 'low' END AS grp,
    SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spend
  FROM invoice_items ii
  JOIN tracks t ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
  JOIN albums al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  JOIN invoices inv ON inv.InvoiceId = ii.InvoiceId
  WHERE al.ArtistId IN (SELECT ArtistId FROM top) OR al.ArtistId IN (SELECT ArtistId FROM low)
  GROUP BY inv.CustomerId,
    CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top) THEN 'top'
         WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM low) THEN 'low' END
),
avgs AS (
  SELECT grp, AVG(spend) AS avg_spend FROM cust_spend GROUP BY grp
)
SELECT ABS(MAX(CASE WHEN grp='top' THEN avg_spend END) - MAX(CASE WHEN grp='low' THEN avg_spend END)) AS abs_diff
FROM avgs;

  SELECT ArtistId FROM artist_sales ORDER BY total_sales ASC, Name ASC LIMIT 1
),
cust_spend AS (
  SELECT inv.CustomerId,
    SUM(CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM top_artist) THEN ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS top_spend,
    SUM(CASE WHEN al.ArtistId = (SELECT ArtistId FROM low_artist) THEN ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS low_spend
  FROM invoice_items ii
  JOIN invoices inv ON inv.InvoiceId = ii.InvoiceId
  JOIN tracks t ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
  JOIN albums al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY inv.CustomerId
),
top_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(top_spend) AS avg_top FROM cust_spend WHERE top_spend > 0
),
low_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(low_spend) AS avg_low FROM cust_spend WHERE low_spend > 0
)
SELECT ABS((SELECT avg_top FROM top_avg) - (SELECT avg_low FROM low_avg)) AS abs_diff
